title: Down and Up: The Phase of a Leg, How Long It Stands and Swings, and Where the Foot Should Come Down

questions.question: What is the duty factor?
options: The time a foot spends on the ground, in seconds
The fraction of the body's weight a foot carries
The fraction of the period a foot is on the ground
The number of feet on the ground at once
questions.explanation: It is a share of the period: with a period of 0.5 s and a duty of 0.5 each foot is down for 0.25 s and in the air for the rest.

questions.question: A walk with a duty of 0.75 always had at least how many feet down?
options: 2, a diagonal pair
4, since a walk never lifts a foot fully
1, while the other three swing in turn
questions.explanation: The legs are a quarter of a cycle apart and each is down for three quarters, so only one is ever up. Three feet can hold a body still.

questions.question: A duty of 0.35 gave a flight phase of:
options: 30 percent
15 percent
35 percent
65 percent
questions.explanation: With the diagonals half a cycle apart and each down for only 0.35, there are two stretches of 0.15 of the period when nothing is down.

questions.question: Raibert's rule puts the foot ahead of the hip by:
options: Half the distance the body goes in the stance, 0.050 m here
The whole distance the body goes in the stance, 0.100 m here
A fixed step length, whatever the speed
The body's speed times the swing time
questions.explanation: Half ahead on landing and half behind on leaving keeps the body centred over the leg's travel: at 0.4 m/s and a stance of 0.25 s, 0.050 m each way.

questions.question: Why does the speed term push the foot forward when the body is too fast?
options: A foot further ahead lengthens the stance
A foot further ahead lifts the body
It keeps the foot from slipping at touchdown
A foot further ahead slows the body
questions.explanation: A foot ahead of the neutral place pushes back on the body during the stance. The term is a small speed controller built into the foot placement.

questions.question: Why can a trot not stand still?
options: Its duty is too short for the legs to carry the weight
Two feet cannot hold a body still, so it balances while moving
Its period is too short for the servos
It can, if the feet are spread wide enough
questions.explanation: Two feet make a line, and a body cannot rest over a line. The trot balances by always falling toward the next pair of feet.
